text:
Predicates:
Visited(x, y) ::: x visited y.
MountainRange(y) ::: y is a mountain range.
LocatedIn(y, z) ::: y is located in z.
Mine(y) ::: y is a mine.
In(y, z) ::: y is in z.
Donated(y) ::: y has been donated.

Premises:
PicurisMountains(y) ∧ MountainRange(y) ∧ LocatedIn(y, NewMexico) ∨ LocatedIn(y, Texas) ::: The Picuris Mountains are a mountain range in New Mexico or Texas.
Visited(JuanDeOnate, y) ::: Juan de Onate visited the Picuris Mountains.
Mine(mine) ∧ LocatedIn(mine, y) ∧ Donated(mine) ::: The Harding Pegmatite Mine, located in the Picuris Mountains, was donated.
∀x ∀y (MountainRange(y) ∧ In(y, Texas) ∧ ∃z (Mine(z) ∧ LocatedIn(z, y) ∧ Donated(z))) → ⊥ ::: There are no mountain ranges in Texas that have mines which have been donated.

Conclusion:
Visited(JuanDeOnate, y) ∧ MountainRange(y) ∧ LocatedIn(y, NewMexico) ::: Juan de Onate visited a mountain range in New Mexico.
